correctness.rationale: In the uniform labelled Bell partition model, for FIXED rank r>=2 and limit E∞ with infinitely many finite classes of each positive size, exact rank-r sentence ∃x_1...∃x_{r-1}∀y says at least r-1 distinct singleton classes. Duplicator survives r rounds if >=r-1 singleton classes and >=r classes of each size j=2..r, matching opened small classes and treating large ones as >=r; a possible rth new singleton on the LAST move can be imitated by an unused nonsingleton. Exact Bell assembly coefficient marks class counts; saddle w exp(w)=n gives for fixed j,t P(N_j=t)~exp(-w^j/j!)(w^j/j!)^t/t!. Thus singleton shortage dominates and P(rank-r failure)~w^(r-1)/((r-2)! n), non-singleton shortages exponentially smaller in w^2. Independently reconstructed Bell and forbidden-singleton recurrences through n=320, checking exact probability mass and decreasing relative-error trends for fixed t; this is finite corroboration, not a proof of the saddle estimate.
